source.title: Semi-flat minima and saddle points by embedding neural networks to overparameterization
source.authors: K. Fukumizu; Shoichiro Yamaguchi; Yoh-ichi Mototake; Mirai Tanaka

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplements are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how adding surplus units changes generalization error in a synthetic regression setting, extending the width–generalization question to ReLU and tanh networks.
record.gate_note: The numerical experiment reports generalization-error changes as hidden units are added. The theoretical embedding and PAC-Bayes arguments are not empirical test-error results.
record.test_reason: The experiment widens an already fitted network by adding inactive units and then perturbs its parameters; it does not train wider networks to convergence and compare their test errors as V2 requires. Its activation-dependent perturbation results and flatness arguments do not test any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the numerical experiment but understates the broader conclusion: the authors characterize minima and saddle points under three embedding methods and suggest that ReLU's additional flat directions may favor generalization when realizing zero training error. They leave implications for learning dynamics to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic one-dimensional regression experiment using inactive-unit embedding and parameter perturbation; optimizer and standard gradient-training recipe are not stated.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation function (ReLU versus tanh) changes whether generalization error increases as surplus units are added.

fits_no_version.finding: After fitting five-unit networks to near-zero squared training error, adding inactive units and perturbing all parameters increases generalization error for tanh, while ReLU shows no such increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization under parameter perturbation can depend on activation function when fitted networks are widened through inactive-unit embedding.

fits_no_version.finding: The analysis gives additional flat directions for embedded ReLU minima and suggests a better PAC-Bayes upper bound than for smooth networks under the specified constructions and distribution choices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inactive-unit embeddings of zero-error ReLU networks can yield flatter minima and more favorable generalization bounds than corresponding smooth-network embeddings.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code is available in Supplements.
record.problems: The empirical result is a synthetic one-dimensional regression experiment with 10 training examples; optimizer details are not stated, and Figure 2(b) provides the plotted values without numerical values in the text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus held-out performance on random and natural labels.
Test-error trends when successively wider ReLU networks are trained to convergence beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps within a convolutional family and comparisons with alternative measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Withdraw the extracted V2 challenge: neither the training comparison nor a stated absence of its predicted improvement is provided. The flatness analysis also does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gaps.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label experiment or natural-label classification result.
The experiment uses synthetic one-dimensional regression data, not MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10; it does not report that ReLU test error keeps lowering as width increases.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with other generalization measures.

relation.reason: The paper discusses overparameterization, flat minima and generalization, but its results do not test or operationally use any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: Inactive-unit embedding and subsequent perturbation do not test V2's comparison of networks trained to convergence at different widths. The theoretical flatness analysis does not test V7's magnitude-aware ranking of generalization gaps.

source_check.notes: Figure 2(b) supplies the error ratios graphically; the prose reports increasing error for tanh and no corresponding increase for ReLU. This does not establish decreasing test error with width.
